newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish tax take rises by 10.5 pct in 1996-officials.
newsitem.headline: Irish tax take rises by 10.5 pct in 1996-officials.

text.p: Irish tax revenue rose by 10.5 percent in 1996, well above budget estimates which predicted a 6.5 percent increase, reflecting the strength of the Irish economy, finance ministry officials said on Friday.

Tax revenue in the full year was 452 million punts ahead of target, contributing to an Exchequer Borrowing Requirement of 437 million punts, an outturn well below the government's official target of 729 million, officials told a news conference following publication of the 1996 Exchequer returns.

"The outturn reflects a continuing strong performance by the Irish economy -- notably in the area of employment, which remains in a very positive phase, generating buoyant tax inflows and reducing the pressures on welfare spending," the finance ministry said in a statement.
Income tax rose by 10.5 percent compared with expectations of a 6.1 percent increase while strong car sales boosted excise by 8.4 percent, officials said.
Corporation tax also posted a strong rise, increasing by 24.4 percent against budget day predictions of a 12.6 percent rise.

Officials said that they now estimate that Irish GNP grew at a rate of 6.25 percent in 1996 while they forecast GDP of 7.25 percent compared with budget day forecasts of 5.0 percent and 5.75 percent respectively.
They also said there were no signs that the Irish economy was running out of steam.
"We are predicting a slightly lower rate of growth for next year than this year," one official said. "But it should be a small rather than a fast slowdown," he said.
He also said the finance ministry was conscious of the need to keep an eye on total demand in the economy.
"We can't be complacent on the subject but there is no evidence coming through of inflationary pressures in the economy," he said.
